title: Anonymous French letter partly in undeciphered secret signs, among the Lubomirski papers of Rákóczi's archive
shelfmark: MNL OL, G 15 (II. Rákóczi Ferenc fejedelem levéltára, Emigrációba vitt rész), Caps. C, Fasc. 39/b, fol. 20
folio_note: One leaf. Neighbours in the fascicle: fol. 14-19 and 21-28 are Latin letters of Theodor Lubomirski and his secretary Georgius Reyscher from Lubló and Podolin, 1705-1708, none with a cipher note.
status: MNL item record (adatlap 15835): language 'Francia', note 'részben megfejtetlen titkos jelekkel' (partly in undeciphered secret signs). Not on DECODE: DECODE's 97 records headed 'Caps. C. why: A cipher of signs (not the number cipher of the Polish correspondence) in the file on Rákóczi's dealings with Lubomirski over the Szepes towns, 1707-08.

verify: Order a scan of Caps. C Fasc. 39/b fol. 20; compare the signs with the sign alphabets among DECODE's G 15 Caps. C Fasc. 43 keys (Láng T.Rak.63 is a key 'with signs').

seen.where: MNL AdatbazisokOnline datasheets (record text only, no images), read 11 Nov 2026: adatlap 15835, with the neighbours 15832-15838.
seen.extent: One leaf (fol. 20); the share in cipher is not stated beyond 'partly'.
seen.cipher: Archive's note, verbatim: 'részben megfejtetlen titkos jelekkel' (Nyelv: Francia; Levélíró N. N.; Címzett N. N.; s.d.; s. l.). The same database writes 'megfejtett', 'egykorúlag megfejtett' or 'Thaly által megfejtett' where a decipherment is on or with the leaf, so 'megfejtetlen' records ciphertext without one.

prior_art.decode: decode_list.py 'G15' lists 290 DECODE records; the 97 from 'Caps. C. Fasc. 39' carry page numbers 115-347, and their dated records fall on Fasc. 39/a folios (three of 16 Jan 1705 at pp. 232-240 = 39/a fol. 145-150; R902 pp. 277-279 = 39/a fol. 171-172; R922 pp. 346-347 = 39/a fol. 212). None is an undated one-leaf French letter in signs; DECODE describes all of them as numerical.
prior_art.tomokiyo: The repo copy of Tomokiyo's unsolved list (unsolved.htm) and the cryptiana index page (code/crypto.htm, fetched 11 Nov 2026) were searched for Lubomirski, Rakoczi and Podolin: no entry on either.
prior_art.lasry: The repo copy of Lasry's publication list (targets/esp318/lit/crypt/GL.htm) was searched for Rakoczi, Lubomirski and Hungary: no Rakoczi or Lubomirski entry, and the web search below named no Lasry paper on this archive.
prior_art.edition: No edition can be matched to an anonymous, undated leaf. Thaly's Archivum Rákóczianum is credited by this database on every leaf he deciphered ('Thaly által megfejtett'); this record carries no 'Kiadási információk' field and no such credit.
prior_art.literature: Láng 2015 (real-d.mtak.hu/922, pdftotext): the repertory row C.Rak.260-360 covers 'MOL G 15 Caps. C Fasc 39 (214 fols, about 100 enciphered letters)', the number cipher of the Polish correspondence, 'solved above the ciphers, mostly'; grep for '39/b' and for Lubomirski in the repertory returns nothing. Láng 2018 (archive.org OCR) has no hit for 39/b either.

title: Two anonymous cipher items next to the undeciphered letters of catalogue 2479, language given only as '[rejtjeles]'
shelfmark: MNL OL, G 15 (II. Rákóczi Ferenc fejedelem levéltára, Emigrációba vitt rész), Caps. A1, Fasc. 11, fol. 61-61/a and fol. 62
folio_note: Two items, about three leaves. Fol. 60 before them is a clear Hungarian letter to 'jó Barátom' described as 'diplomáciai témáról, rejtjelezés továbbításáról szóló ... szándékosan homályosan (nevek és adatok nélkül) fogalmazott levél' (on forwarding an encipherment).
status: MNL item records 13650 and 13651: 'Nyelv: [rejtjeles]', writer and addressee N. N., no note and no decipherment recorded. The catalogued siblings fol. 36-37 and 46-47 (catalogue 2479) have the same language value with the note 'végig megfejtetlen rejtjeles levél'; these two were left out of the first pass because they have no note. why: They belong to the same group of anonymous cipher letters in Rákóczi's private fascicle as catalogue 2479 and add ciphertext to it.

date: 21 Oct 1707, 10 Dec 1707 (two exemplars), 17 Dec 1707, 13 Jan 1708, 17 Feb 1708; and 4 Jan 1708
title: Jakab Kray, Rákóczi's agent at Danzig: duplicates and triplicates of his number-cipher reports that were only partly deciphered
correspondents: Jakab Kray → Francis II Rákóczi (one as 'Pompeius Cettoni')
shelfmark: MNL OL, G 15 (II. Rákóczi Ferenc fejedelem levéltára, Emigrációba vitt rész), Caps. D, Fasc. 83, fol. 26-27, 57-58, 59-60, 71-72; Fasc. 84, fol. 17-18, 25-26; and Fasc. 84, fol. 7-12
folio_note: Seven items, about 18 leaves. Each of the first six has a same-date exemplar marked 'végig megfejtett számjelekkel': Fasc. 83 fol. 28-29 (21 Oct), 66-67 (10 Dec), 69-70 (17 Dec), 87-88 (13 Jan 1708), Fasc. 84 fol. 22-23 (17 Feb, with a transcript at fol. 33r-v). Fasc. 84 fol. 7-12 (4 Jan 1708) has no same-date sibling; its note 'kisebb részben megfejtett számjelekkel' may mean only that a lesser part of the letter is in cipher.
status: MNL item notes: fol. 26-27 and Fasc. 84 fol. 17-18 'csak részben megfejtett számjelekkel'; Fasc. 83 fol. 57-58 (triplicate, No. 25) 'csak részben megfejtett számjelekkel'; fol. 59-60 (duplicate, No. 24) and fol. 71-72 (duplicate, No. 28) 'csak kis részében megfejtett számjelekkel'; Fasc. 84 fol. 25-26 (duplicate, No. 45) 'csak a második szövegrészben megfejtett számjelekkel'. Not on DECODE (no record from Caps. D Fasc. 83-84; search 'Kray' 0).
why: Kray ran Rákóczi's Baltic finance and correspondence; the deciphered exemplars of the same dates give the plaintext, so these leaves are key material for his number cipher more than unread text.
score_note: Scored from the archive's item description during the 11 Nov 2026 second MNL AdatbazisokOnline pass (research/sweep_2026-11-11_mnl_2/); not viewed (no images online)
verify: Order the pairs (e.g. Fasc. 83 fol. 26-27 with 28-29) and check whether the partly deciphered exemplar has the same text as the fully deciphered one; if so close as read, and keep Fasc. 84 fol. 7-12 only if cipher stands undeciphered on it.

title: János Pápai and Ferenc Horváth to Rákóczi, Constantinople 24 July 1706: a separate slip in undeciphered number cipher
correspondents: János Pápai and Ferenc Horváth → Francis II Rákóczi
shelfmark: MNL OL, G 15 (II. Rákóczi Ferenc fejedelem levéltára, Emigrációba vitt rész), Caps. C, Fasc. 33, fol. 44-49
folio_note: Six leaves; the letter is mostly deciphered, the undeciphered part is a separate slip (cédula). By date this is DECODE R814 ('Caps. C. Fasc. 33. 80-86', 24 Jul 1706, 7 images, status Decrypted).
status: MNL item note (adatlap 15654): 'nagyrészt megfejtett, külön cédulán megfejtetlen számjelekkel'. DECODE R814 is marked Decrypted with inline plaintext; whether the slip is among its seven images was not checked (images need a DECODE login).
why: A postscript slip of the Constantinople envoys left unread by Rákóczi's chancery; the envoys' key (DECODE R580, used in targets/papai1706) should read it.
score_note: Scored from the archive's item description during the 11 Nov 2026 second MNL AdatbazisokOnline pass (research/sweep_2026-11-11_mnl_2/); not viewed (no images online)
verify: Open DECODE R814 with a login, find the slip, decode it with the R580 key table of targets/papai1706; it belongs with that target rather than in the catalogue as a new entry.

title: Rákóczi to an unnamed correspondent, 26 March 1710: French copy with a few words in secret numerals
shelfmark: MNL OL, G 15 (II. Rákóczi Ferenc fejedelem levéltára, Emigrációba vitt rész), Caps. H, Fasc. 229, fol. 186-187
folio_note: Two leaves, a contemporary copy; only a few words are in cipher.
status: MNL item record (adatlap 18322): 'Fennmaradási forma: Egykorú másolat', note 'néhány szó titkos számjegyekkel' (a few words in secret numerals); the note does not say whether they are deciphered. Not on DECODE (no record from Caps. H Fasc. 229).
why: A few enciphered names in a letter of the prince from the last year of the war; Rákóczi's French keys survive (DECODE, G 15 Caps. C Fasc. 43-44), so this is a key lookup once seen.

verify: Order fol. 186-187 and read the numerals with Rákóczi's French keys on DECODE; no block because the note does not show that the words are undeciphered.
